target_customer: Bitcoin buyers and sellers, with a pitch aimed at lower cost cross-border remittances
problem: Early bitcoin exchanges were unreliable and expensive. Buttercoin offered an open source, high volume trading engine and marketplace for bitcoin trades.
business_model: Exchange and marketplace taking trading fees

founders.name: Bennett Hoffman
founders.background_notes: Listed as the only founder on the YC page. TechCrunch did not name founders. No background found.

exit.reason: The company said it could not raise new funding because of a dip in bitcoin interest among Silicon Valley investors. It was solvent and returned user balances. Service ended April 10, 2015.

competitors.name: Coinbase
competitors.what: Bitcoin wallet and exchange, YC S12
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the cited post
competitors.funding_then: 5 million dollar Series A led by Union Square Ventures after a 600,000 dollar seed in September 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: A high volume order book matching engine that handles real money and bitcoin custody is hard and security critical for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The trading engine was open source, so the code itself was not a moat, and exchanges compete on liquidity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch describes market consolidation led by Coinbase and BitPay that made it harder for small exchanges; the company shut down in April 2015.

market_need_then: Bitcoin interest and venture funding rose through 2013 and exchange options were limited. Remittance cost reduction was the stated aim at the August 2013 launch.

branding.domain_note: Exact buttercoin.com, which returned a 503 error when fetched. A BUTTERCOIN trademark filed in May 2014 by Digital Currencies Fintech Co. of Palo Alto is recorded as dead.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by CoinDesk, TechCrunch, The Next Web and Bitcoinist, mostly at the shutdown.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly, memorable name with bitcoin trade press, but most coverage is the shutdown and no community evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: Buttercoin launched in August 2013 and raised about 1.25 to 1.6 million dollars from Google Ventures, YC, Centralway and angels. After bitcoin prices and Silicon Valley interest fell in 2014, it could not raise another round and shut down on April 10, 2015 while still solvent. TechCrunch also pointed to consolidation around Coinbase and BitPay.
notes: CoinDesk article pages returned errors or a login redirect, so the 2013 rounds (1 million from Google Ventures, YC and Alexis Ohanian; 250K from Centralway in September 2013) come from search result summaries of CoinDesk and are single outlet figures. TechCrunch says 1.6 million total with investors Kevin Rose, Chris Hutchins, Floodgate, Initialized and Rothenberg Ventures that are not tied to specific rounds; CB Insights says 1.25 million; CoinDesk's headline says 2.1 million while its body says at least 1.3 million. The gap between rounds recorded (1.25M) and the TechCrunch total is unresolved. The Coinbase post is dated May 2013, before the batch. The company site returned a 503.
